title: AI-based longitudinal monitoring of the dialysis shunt using smartphone-generated audio data: ShuntMerlin
summary:
This study investigates whether sounds recorded from a dialysis shunt using a smartphone can help detect problems at an early stage. Participants attend their regular medical check-ups, where the shunt is examined using ultrasound. In addition, they record short audio clips of their shunt at home once a week using an app.

The collected sound recordings are compared with the ultrasound results to identify patterns that may indicate complications such as narrowing or blockage. The goal is to develop a digital tool that can support early detection and improve patient care in the future.

interventions.name:
The ShuntMerlin study is a multicenter, non-interventional observational study investigating the correlation between smartphone-based audio recordings of dialysis shunts and sonographic findings.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Legally competent patients who have been informed about the study in written and oral form and have provided informed consent to participate.
Women and men over 18 years of age with a native forearm arteriovenous shunt (so-called Cimino fistula/radiocephalic AV fistula), either left- or right-sided.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients with prosthetic shunts (e.g., PTFE grafts, AngioSeal®, Goretex®).
Patients with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs).
Patients with severe valvular heart disease.
Dependent patients under care.
